newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - still flat, still nervous.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - still flat, still nervous.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds remained largely unchanged in early afternoon trade on Friday as the market looked ahead to the March 25 central bank meeting, at which it was expected to raise interest rates.

"The market is trading very nervous," a trader said. "Mr. Greenspan keeps threatening to tighten...and everybody is waiting to see how the market reacts," he added, referring to the chairman of the Federal Reserve, who on Thursday, in his Congressional testimony, reinforced views that he likely would press for a rate increase.
The Federal Reserve bank's policy-making body's next regularly scheduled meeting is March 25, and Chairman Alan Greenspan has repeatedly said he wanted to act pre-emptively to ward off any inflation.

Even though Fridays typicaly are slow trading days, traders said that activity was fairly decent, in part because a fair number of bid-wanted lists were being circulated and bargain-hunters were out looking.

"We've seen a small bid from clients trying to pick up good structure at these levels," the trader said. He noted that one gauge of the secondary market, Standard and Poor's Corp Blue List, totaled over $1.6 billion, a robust level.
While new issuance next week was expected to slip to around $1.7 billion, traders noted that volume has been fairly high in the past few weeks, which has swelled some players' inventories.

In the secondary market, Dade County, Florida, Water and Sewer System Revenues of October 2026, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.79 percent, NET, down two basis points. And the Jefferson County, Alabama, Sewer Revenues of February 2022, which have a 5-5/8 percent coupon, were bid at 5.87 percent, unchanged.

In the futures markets, the June U.S. Treasury bond futures fell two ticks to 108-5/32, while the June municipal bond futures gained nine ticks to 113-2/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 157 ticks.
